title: Opus X chosen for recording; Dizzy's solo over the bridge
summary: Eckstine picks Malachi's teenage-era Opus X, and Dizzy adds a soaring solo over the bridge's big chords.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Charlie Parker: encounters, lore and legacy

blocks.x: And I was very happy...I was amazed when we were preparing for this record date, that Billy Eckstine came to me and said, "John, for this record date that we're going to do, we're going to record your arrangement, your tune." I had written a thing called "Opus X" for the band. Actually, "Opus X" was written back when I was a teenager for this little band that we had, and I later played it with Tommy Miles' band. It had two or three different names. So when I wrote it for Billy Eckstine, I wrote it simply as something to help out this scarcity of arrangements that we had. I didn't really think that much of it. But with the help of Charlie Parker and Dizzy again, it turned out to be a much better sounding tune.
The way that happened was, when we first rehearsed it, I had a thing in the bridge at first, where I just had the saxes

and the brass section build it up with some big chords, and it started off kind of quiet and they'd build up to a climax at the end of 8 bars of the bridge. Well, when we rehearsed it, Dizzy took a solo in that particular part over all the top of this to-do that the band was playing. Which gave it another spark, because he came in and he played... The bridge had a lot of augmented eleventh chords in it and thirteenths and whatnot, and he just was right over the top of it. Dizzy had a real thing for getting over the top of a whole band playing, and just soar, you know. So that added something to it.
